newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin policies could jeopardise euro - Balladur.
newsitem.headline: Jospin policies could jeopardise euro - Balladur.

text.p: Former conservative prime minister Edouard Balladur said on Friday the Socialist-led government's policies would cost 50 billion francs ($8.6 billion) and jeopardise France's plans to join a single European currency.

Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, swept to power this month, outlined his policies to parliament on Thursday including job creation and shorter working hours. He said he was committed to joining the euro from 1999 but gave no estimate of how his policies would affect the budget.

"I didn't hear...any talk of reducing public spending," Balladur told Europe 1 radio. "On the contrary, it is going to be raised." He said that the measures unveiled by Jospin represent "a good 50 billion francs".
"That's not the way to revive growth. It's the opposite of what needs to be done," said Balladur, who was prime minister from 1993-95.
"France has a big interest in entering in Europe and building the single currency," said Balladur.
"In the current state of things, if spending is raised, if our social system is rigidified still further, I don't see how we will be able to stick to our European ambitions," he said.
France needs to cut its deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 to qualify for the euro from 1999.
